location.name: Berth four

view.text: Berth four. The Patience knocks the pilings. The shack window is lit.

charview.label: Marsh
charview.text: Marsh keeps his clear eye on you and the clouded one on the shack.
charview.conversation: "The book is on the table. Leave the floor. Read the hour to the woman up the hill." His key goes into your hand. "The rain is not a room."
He does not turn. "You heard me. The table, not the floor."
"Olive, with brass buttons? A tide clerk's coat. He's still wearing his, then." He looks up the lane. "Penry at the board will have seen him go up."
"She stays tied till his name's read somewhere dry." He pats the rail. "Penry keeps the sluice chain up on Bakery Row. Tell him: a dry room."
"Voss. Kept the tide at the harbour office. Ask there what hour he wrote down."
Marsh puts a palm between the ledger and the deck. "Dry room. Her voice waiting. Not this boat, and not this fog."

view.text: The pier head. The harbour office has one lit window. The lane climbs into fog.

location.asset: You kneel at the edge. Between the pilings something pale turns, the size of a face, and the tide takes it.
You look again. The harbour keeps what it turned.
location.ending: You read his hour to the harbour. The pale face turns up between the pilings and does not go back under.
location.asset: Marsh turns on the deck. His clear eye takes you in; the clouded one stays on the shack. "You're the one she hired."
"He kept the tide. He came down for his hour and did not come up." He nods at the shack without looking at it. "Nothing went in the water from this deck. Ask me about the floor if you want the rest."
"You looked, then. Then you know what the floor in there opens on. Same water. Nearer." He does not say the name. "Ask me about the floor."
A brass padlock through the hasp, the kind the Patience uses on her lockers. The window is lit for nobody. The mate has the key.
Marsh's key turns stiffly. The padlock drops open in your hand, and the door gives onto lamplight.
You read his hour to the lane. The fog takes the words. Something matches your step and does not fall behind.

view.text: The hill lamp is a smear in the fog. A man in a wet coat keeps a few planks ahead.

location.ending: You pass him and climb. Edith waits in the chair. The hour was spoken in the rain, and she does not open the locket. He is still on the stair.
You go to him. The face from the folder looks back through the rain, and he does not speak. The hill does not take you.
